title: Modal verbs 5: had to / was able to / managed to
note: a2_could_able gave past ability COULD. This is the rest: had to for past obligation (must has no past), and was able to / managed to for a single occasion that succeeded, where could does not work. Czech musel jsem -> *I must yesterday. Czech podarilo se mi is the managed to slot. Thickened 10 -> 25 items 2026-09-04 (agent loop): had to, didn't have to, Did ... have to, wasn't/weren't able to, managed to, and two could items for the general ability contrast card 2 teaches. Rules applied this pass: A4 all five cleared - three by giving the Czech the demonstrative it really uses (ty dvere, ten listek, tu posledni otazku), two by rewriting onto a taxi / a cheap hotel / just in time; F3 `fix` swapped for `start`. F6: the obligation items now run on rotated noun subjects (my parents, my sister, my brother, my friends, my son, my neighbour) instead of a column of pronouns. KNOWN LINT FALSE POSITIVE: A8 asks for the contraction twin of `I had to work` (*I'd to work) and `Did you have to wait` (*Did you've to wait). Neither is English, so neither is in accepts and the two flags stand. Queued in DECISIONS.md - the fix is a guard in lint.py, not in this pack. Do not `fix` these by adding the accepts. · 2026-09-05 James smoke: C6 — the Job column defined had to as "you were obliged to do it" (obliged is C1). Jobs rewritten in A1 words, and per C58 the table now carries an Example column so the form is shown in a sentence beside its meaning. Card 3 no longer says "forbidden". · 2026-09-05 James smoke, second pass: "difference between could and were able to is not clear (and often not really important)" and "this question is no good". Card 2 now says the two are the SAME for known ability and in every negative, and part company only for one thing done on one occasion. The contrast was never actually tested: all five be-able-to items cue (be able) in brackets, so only items 23/24 asked the student to choose — and both offered a second right answer (was able / Were you able, which was also ungrammatical against the stem). Those chips are now clearly-wrong forms of the same word, keeping *Did you could* as the unit's own error (B4). couldn't added to accepts on the two negatives where the frame allows it. Four of the seven identical *had to* affirmatives cut: 25 -> 21 items. · 2026-09-05 James smoke, third pass: "ambiguity and tenses are key here". B27 — nothing in the English said these sentences were past, so the Czech was the only carrier and *He doesn't have to work on Saturday* was as good an answer as *didn't*. The 17 stems with no past anchor now carry `/ past` in the cue (b1_it_subject's convention: `(nice / past)` -> It was nice). Items 0, 7, 19 and 20 anchor in the sentence itself (last Saturday, her car broke down, when I was five, when you were a child) and keep their bare cues — the bracket names only what the stem cannot. A5 — *were able to* and *managed to* are interchangeable on a single occasion that succeeded ("I would accept either"), so the twin is in accepts on all seven such items and each explanation says so, the same way 14/15 already say *couldn't* is just as good. Type stays determinate: the (be able) / (manage) cue still picks one. Lint 0 EXACT after.

cards.title: Modal verbs 5: had to / was able to / managed to
cards.title_cz: Modální slovesa 5: had to / was able to / managed to
points: These are the **modal verbs** you already know, in the past.
**must** has no past form at all. It borrows **had to**.

examples.cz: Podařilo se jí skončit před šestou.

cards.title: The three past forms
points: **managed to** adds the idea that it took effort.

rows: you could do it, and you did it that time
I **was able** to open the door.
it was hard, and you did it

cards.title: could, or was able to?
points: Only the last row is a difference. Everywhere else, take either one.
For one thing you did on one occasion, use **was able** to or **managed to**.

rows: what you knew how to do
I **could** read when I was five.
I **was able** to read when I was five.
We **weren't able** to open the door.
one thing you did, one time
He **was able** to start the car.

cards.title: Negatives and questions
points: **didn't have** to means you had a choice. It does not mean *do not do it*.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: **must** cannot go in the past. Say **had to**.

rows: I **managed to** pass the exam yesterday.

blocks.title: Modal verbs 5: had to / was able to / managed to

items.en: I had to work last Saturday.
items.cz: Musel jsem v sobotu pracovat.
items.gap: I ____ work last Saturday. (must)
accepts: I had to work last Saturday.
items.wrong: I must work last Saturday.
items.explanation: **must** has no past. The past of must is **had to**.
items.explanation_cz: **must** nemá minulý čas. Minulý čas od must je **had to**.

items.en: She managed to finish before six.
items.cz: Podařilo se jí skončit před šestou.
items.gap: She ____ finish before six. (manage / past)
accepts: She managed to finish before six.
She was able to finish before six.
items.wrong: She could finish before six.
items.explanation: One occasion, and it was an effort: **managed to** finish. *was able to* is just as good English here.
items.explanation_cz: Jedna příležitost a stálo to úsilí: **managed to** finish. *was able to* je tady stejně dobrá angličtina.

items.en: We weren't able to open the door.
items.cz: Nedokázali jsme ty dveře otevřít.
items.gap: We ____ to open the door. (not / be able / past)
accepts: We weren't able to open the door.
We were not able to open the door.
items.wrong: We didn't able to open the door.
items.explanation: **be able to** keeps the be verb: weren't **able to**.
items.explanation_cz: **be able to** si drží sloveso be: weren't **able to**.

items.en: Did you have to wait long?
items.cz: Musel jsi dlouho čekat?
items.gap: ____ wait long? (you / have to / past)
accepts: Did you have to wait long?
items.wrong: Did you must wait long?
items.explanation: Questions with **have to** use **did**: Did you have to wait.
items.explanation_cz: Otázky s **have to** používají **did**: Did you have to wait.

items.en: I didn't have to pay for the ticket.
items.cz: Za ten lístek jsem platit nemusel.
items.gap: I ____ pay for the ticket. (not / have to / past)
accepts: I didn't have to pay for the ticket.
I did not have to pay for the ticket.
items.explanation: **didn't have to** = it was not necessary. **mustn't** would mean it was forbidden.
items.explanation_cz: **didn't have to** = nebylo to nutné. **mustn't** by znamenalo, že to bylo zakázáno.

items.en: He was able to start the car himself.
items.cz: Dokázal to auto nastartovat sám.
items.gap: He ____ start the car himself. (be able / past)
accepts: He was able to start the car himself.
He managed to start the car himself.
items.explanation: **he** takes **was able to**, one job that he completed. *managed to* is just as good English here.
items.explanation_cz: **he** má **was able to**, jedna věc, kterou dotáhl. *managed to* je tady stejně dobrá angličtina.
items.wrong: He was can start the car himself.

items.en: I managed to get a ticket just in time.
items.cz: Na poslední chvíli se mi podařilo sehnat lístek.
items.gap: I ____ get a ticket just in time. (manage / past)
accepts: I managed to get a ticket just in time.
I was able to get a ticket just in time.
items.explanation: It was difficult and it worked: **managed to** get. *was able to* is just as good English here.
items.explanation_cz: Bylo to těžké a povedlo se: **managed to** get. *was able to* je tady stejně dobrá angličtina.
items.wrong: I could get a ticket just in time.

items.en: My sister had to take a taxi because her car broke down.
items.cz: Sestra musela jet taxíkem, protože se jí porouchalo auto.
items.gap: My sister ____ take a taxi because her car broke down. (must)
accepts: My sister had to take a taxi because her car broke down.
items.wrong: My sister must take a taxi because her car broke down.
items.explanation: **she** + past obligation: had to take.
items.explanation_cz: **she** + minulá povinnost: had to take.

items.en: We were able to find a cheap hotel.
items.cz: Podařilo se nám najít levný hotel.
items.gap: We ____ find a cheap hotel. (be able / past)
accepts: We were able to find a cheap hotel.
We managed to find a cheap hotel.
items.explanation: **we** takes **were able to** for a single search that succeeded. *managed to* is just as good English here.
items.explanation_cz: **we** má **were able to** pro jedno hledání, které vyšlo. *managed to* je tady stejně dobrá angličtina.
items.wrong: We could to find a cheap hotel.

items.en: My son had to study all weekend.
items.cz: Syn se musel učit celý víkend.
items.gap: My son ____ study all weekend. (must / past)
accepts: My son had to study all weekend.
items.wrong: My son must study all weekend.
items.explanation: **had to** is the past of both *must* and *have to*.
items.explanation_cz: **had to** je minulý tvar od *must* i od *have to*.

items.en: Did your friends have to pay for parking?
items.cz: Museli kamarádi platit za parkování?
items.gap: ____ pay for parking? (your friends / have to / past)
accepts: Did your friends have to pay for parking?
items.wrong: Did your friends must pay for parking?
items.explanation: The question is built with **did** + have to. *did must* is never English.
items.explanation_cz: Otázka se tvoří s **did** + have to. *did must* v angličtině neexistuje.

items.en: Did she have to change trains?
items.cz: Musela přestupovat?
items.gap: ____ change trains? (she / have to / past)
accepts: Did she have to change trains?
items.wrong: Must she change trains?
items.explanation: Past question: **Did** she **have to**…? *Must she* asks about now.
items.explanation_cz: Minulá otázka: **Did** she **have to**…? *Must she* se ptá na přítomnost.

items.en: You didn't have to come so early.
items.cz: Nemusel jsi chodit tak brzo.
items.gap: You ____ come so early. (not / have to / past)
accepts: You didn't have to come so early.
You did not have to come so early.
items.wrong: You mustn't come so early.
items.explanation: **didn't have to** = it was not necessary. *mustn't* would mean it was forbidden.
items.explanation_cz: **didn't have to** = nebylo to nutné. *mustn't* by znamenalo, že to bylo zakázané.

items.en: He didn't have to work on Saturday.
items.cz: V sobotu pracovat nemusel.
items.gap: He ____ work on Saturday. (not / have to / past)
accepts: He didn't have to work on Saturday.
He did not have to work on Saturday.
items.wrong: He mustn't work on Saturday.
items.explanation: Not necessary, not forbidden: **didn't have to** work.
items.explanation_cz: Nebylo to nutné, ne zakázané: **didn't have to** work.

items.en: I wasn't able to answer the last question.
items.cz: Na tu poslední otázku jsem nedokázal odpovědět.
items.gap: I ____ answer the last question. (not / be able / past)
accepts: I wasn't able to answer the last question.
I was not able to answer the last question.
I couldn't answer the last question.
I could not answer the last question.
items.wrong: I didn't able to answer the last question.
items.explanation: The negative sits on **be**: **wasn't able to**. *didn't able* has two verbs. **I couldn't answer** is just as good English here.
items.explanation_cz: Zápor je na **be**: **wasn't able to**. *didn't able* má dvě slovesa proti sobě.

items.en: We weren't able to book a table.
items.cz: Nepodařilo se nám zamluvit stůl.
items.gap: We ____ book a table. (not / be able / past)
accepts: We weren't able to book a table.
We were not able to book a table.
We couldn't book a table.
We could not book a table.
items.wrong: We wasn't able to book a table.
items.explanation: **we** takes **weren't** able to. The rest of the frame does not change. **We couldn't book** is just as good English here.
items.explanation_cz: **we** má **weren't** able to. Zbytek vazby se nemění.

items.en: She managed to pass her exam.
items.cz: Podařilo se jí udělat zkoušku.
items.gap: She ____ pass her exam. (manage / past)
accepts: She managed to pass her exam.
She was able to pass her exam.
items.wrong: She could pass her exam.
items.explanation: One exam, and it was hard: **managed to** pass. *could* would mean a general ability. *was able to* is just as good English here.
items.explanation_cz: Jedna zkouška a bylo to těžké: **managed to** pass. *could* by znamenalo obecnou schopnost. *was able to* je tady stejně dobrá angličtina.

items.en: They managed to find a cheap flat.
items.cz: Podařilo se jim najít levný byt.
items.gap: They ____ find a cheap flat. (manage / past)
accepts: They managed to find a cheap flat.
They were able to find a cheap flat.
items.wrong: They could find a cheap flat.
items.explanation: A single success after some effort: **managed to** find. *were able to* is just as good English here.
items.explanation_cz: Jeden úspěch po nějaké námaze: **managed to** find. *were able to* je tady stejně dobrá angličtina.

items.en: I managed to finish everything before lunch.
items.cz: Podařilo se mi všechno dodělat před obědem.
items.gap: I ____ finish everything before lunch. (manage / past)
accepts: I managed to finish everything before lunch.
I was able to finish everything before lunch.
items.wrong: I could finish everything before lunch.
items.explanation: **managed to** says it took effort and it worked. *could* cannot report one finished occasion. *was able to* is just as good English here.
items.explanation_cz: **managed to** říká, že to dalo práci a povedlo se. *could* neumí popsat jednu hotovou situaci. *was able to* je tady stejně dobrá angličtina.

items.en: I could read when I was five.
items.cz: Uměl jsem číst, když mi bylo pět.
items.gap: I ____ read when I was five. (can)
accepts: I could read when I was five.
items.wrong: I managed to read when I was five.
items.explanation: A general ability over years is **could**. *managed to* is for one hard occasion.
items.explanation_cz: Obecná schopnost po léta je **could**. *managed to* je pro jednu těžkou situaci.

items.en: Could you swim when you were a child?
items.cz: Uměl jsi plavat, když jsi byl malý?
items.gap: ____ swim when you were a child? (you / can)
accepts: Could you swim when you were a child?
items.wrong: Did you could swim when you were a child?
items.explanation: General ability in a question: **Could you**…? No *did* in front of a modal.
items.explanation_cz: Obecná schopnost v otázce: **Could you**…? Před modálním slovesem není *did*.
